ADAPTATION (Component Overhaul):
- Objective: Major behavioral adjustment to fix localized stagnation.
- Scope: Completely rewrite the system prompts of lagging or failing agents. Swap, add, or deprecate specific tools.
- Invariance: Maintain the structural routing/topology of the multi-agent graph.
- Strategy: Retain the overall workflow architecture, but radically re-engineer how individual nodes think and execute.

EXPLORATION (Macro Structural Mutation):
- Objective: Break out of a severe local minimum or chronic structural failure.
- Scope: Mutate the graph topology. Add a new specialized agent, merge two redundant agents, or change the routing logic.
- Invariance: Keep the fundamental task goal, but completely change the operational workflow.
- Strategy: Restructure the cognitive pipeline. Introduce parallel processing, voting consensus, or multi-step validation loops.

RE-SPECIATION (Systemic Paradigm Shift):
- Objective: The current evolutionary branch is a dead end. Escape entirely.
- Scope: Clean-slate redesign of the multi-agent architecture.
- Invariance: None. Only the core task description and learned constraints/task specifications remain constant.
- Strategy: Rethink the entire approach. If it was a sequential pipeline, turn it into an autonomous swarm. If it was highly fragmented, design a single ultra-dense prompt. Radical experimentation.

- Strategy: Focus heavily on clarifying the input/output boundaries and communication contracts between agents.
